key_insight: Quantum circuit simulation cost is strongly family-dependent, and a family-aware residual model can predict both approximation threshold and runtime from OpenQASM plus context.
engineering_relevance: This lets practitioners choose simulation settings in milliseconds instead of running expensive trial-and-error sweeps that can take minutes to hours.
method: Shared neural backbone reads circuit structure and execution context.
Pretrained family classifier adds algorithm-specific residual corrections for QFT/Grover/VQE-like families.
Domain heuristics provide fingerprint features for gate composition and entanglement-related behavior.
evidence_signal: On 7–130 qubit circuits across 10 families, the system reaches 79.5% exact threshold accuracy, 91.2% within one rung, and runtime prediction with R² = 0.82, while inference takes about 50 ms.
watch_item: Performance may depend on reliable family classification and coverage of the training families; unseen circuit patterns could reduce calibration quality.
paper_title: Family-Aware Residual Architecture for Predicting Quantum Circuit Simulation Performance
